content.text:
### Overview

Rankings currently return exactly four complete **top-ten snapshots**, selected by reporting period. “Show more” needs both backend and frontend changes: the Rust service discards rows beyond ten, and the frontend parser explicitly rejects longer boards.

### How It Works

`GET /rankings?period=…` calls `RankingsService::rankings()`. The repository loads all declarations in the period with one `sqlx::query!`; there is no SQL ranking limit. The service aggregates them using `PeriodAggregate`, sorts each board by exact GBP total descending, breaks ties by stable entity ID, and applies `.take(10)`.

The SvelteKit server load validates `period` and `category`, fetches all four boards, and parses exact decimal strings. The page chooses the selected board and passes presentation rows to shared `RankingList`. Its keyed `<ol>` already supports arbitrary row counts, continuous numbering and insertion animations.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Load["+page.server.ts"] --> Adapter["server/rankings.ts"]
  Adapter --> API["HTTP rankings handler"]
  API --> Service["aggregate → sort → take 10"]
  Service --> Repo["all declarations in period"]
  Load --> Page["+page.svelte"]
  Page --> Rows["rankingRows"]
  Rows --> List["RankingList"]
```

### Pagination Precedent

`frontend/src/routes/updates/+page.svelte` already implements the requested interaction: full lists arrive through SSR, the feature initially slices ten rows, and its shared `Button` reveals ten more. Category/sort changes reset visibility. The button disappears at exhaustion and moves focus into new results when the final click removes the button.

This is the smallest existing pattern to follow: retain all ranked rows in the backend response, remove the parser’s ten-row cap, and progressively reveal ten client-side. It preserves one-snapshot consistency without introducing API pagination. True network pagination would need a new request/response contract because none exists for rankings.

### Where Things Live

- `exposed/src/lib/domain/services/rankings.rs`: `top()`, sorting, `.take(10)`, top-ten unit test.
- `exposed/src/lib/domain/models/rankings.rs`: four board vectors; comments promise top ten.
- `exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/handlers/rankings.rs`: serializes board vectors unchanged.
- `exposed/src/lib/outbound/rankings.rs`: declaration query; likely unchanged for progressive reveal.
- `frontend/src/lib/server/rankings.ts`: `board()` rejects lengths over ten.
- `frontend/src/lib/rankings.ts`: board types and exact display/bar calculation.
- `frontend/src/routes/rankings/+page.svelte`: owns category, visible rows and Show more interaction.
- `frontend/src/lib/ui/RankingList.svelte`: existing list contract likely needs no change.
- `frontend/tests/rankings.spec.ts`, `rankings-fixtures.ts`, `loader-adapters.spec.ts`: initial ten, further batches, exhaustion, category/period resets and parser coverage.
- `exposed/src/lib/outbound/rankings/tests.rs`: HTTP bounded-board assertions.
- `frontend/tests/periods.spec.ts`: URL/history/reporting-period behavior.

### Gotchas

- MPs include all declaration categories. Individuals/companies/parties include only donation/support. Preserve this distinction.
- “Companies” includes every canonical non-individual funder kind.
- Party grouping uses recipients’ latest stored party; parties have no entity link, so final-batch focus handling cannot assume links exist.
- Null totals sort last; ties use ID; amounts must remain exact strings.
- Category navigation is URL-backed and uses committed `data.period` during pending navigation. Visibility should reset on the committed category/period change.
- Existing `PeriodSelector` strips `page`, `from` and `to`.
- Existing tests explicitly assert no Show more button on exhausted fixture boards; expand fixtures to exercise >10 rows.
- Calculate bars from the full ranking before slicing if using progressive reveal, to avoid changing scale as rows appear.
- Read UI reference/composition docs before implementation; use shared `Button`, feature-owned pagination state and token spacing. No new explanatory copy is needed.
